properties.vocals: Lead vocals are delivered by Wesley Schultz with a warm, slightly raw baritone timbre; the band relies heavily on close harmonies, group/gang vocals, call-and-response and emotive, story-driven phrasing. Vocal production is typically intimate and unadorned to emphasize lyrics.
properties.biography: Wesley Schultz and Jeremiah Fraites founded The Lumineers in the mid-2000s and developed a direct, acoustic-driven songwriting approach that foregrounded story-based lyrics and communal-sounding choruses. After years of small-venue touring and developing their sound with a rotating cast of players, the band released a self-titled debut album in 2012 whose single "Ho Hey" became a global hit. The group expanded their palette on subsequent records—Cleopatra (2016), the concept-driven III (2019) and Brightside (2022)—while maintaining a focus on raw, singalong arrangements, cello and piano textures, and themes of loss, home and resilience. Touring has been central to their identity, with energetic, participatory live shows that feature stomps, handclaps and close harmonies.
properties.known_for: Rustic acoustic arrangements, emotive storytelling lyrics, rousing sing-along choruses and the international hit "Ho Hey," plus energetic, participatory live performances.
properties.description: The Lumineers are an American folk-rock band built around songwriters Wesley Schultz and Jeremiah Fraites. Formed in the mid-2000s and based in the U.S., they rose to international prominence with the 2012 breakout single "Ho Hey." Their music blends acoustic instrumentation, prominent percussion stomps, cello and piano textures, close vocal harmonies and narrative, emotionally direct lyrics. Major studio albums include The Lumineers (2012), Cleopatra (2016), III (2019) and Brightside (2022).
properties.cultural_impact: The Lumineers helped bring indie-folk and roots-based songwriting into mainstream pop radio in the 2010s, popularizing stripped-down arrangements, communal singalongs and acoustic-driven anthems; their breakout "Ho Hey" became a cultural touchstone and expanded commercial opportunities for Americana and indie-folk acts.
properties.performance_style: Live shows emphasize communal participation (stomps, handclaps, singalongs), intimate storytelling, stripped instrumentation and cinematic dynamics that build to anthemic choruses.

properties.biography: Born on December 8, 1979, in Staten Island, New York, Ingrid Michaelson grew up in the New York City area and studied at Binghamton University. She began performing in the New York independent music scene and self-released early recordings before gaining broader attention in the mid-2000s. Her song placements in television programs and an Old Navy commercial helped elevate tracks such as "The Way I Am" into wider public awareness. Over the following years she released multiple studio albums, toured extensively in small-to-mid-sized venues, and established a reputation for intimate, piano- and guitar-based indie-pop songs with candid, emotionally direct lyrics.

Her catalog balances light, catchy hooks with introspective, conversational lyrics.

properties.biography: Formed in 2009 in Seattle, The Head and the Heart began as a collaboration between Josiah Johnson and Jonathan Russell, who met while attending college. They were soon joined by other members including Charity Rose Thielen, Chris Zasche, Tyler Williams, and Kenny Hensley. The band quickly gained attention for their heartfelt lyrics and harmonious vocals, releasing their self-titled debut album in 2011. Over the years, they have toured extensively and released several albums, solidifying their place in the indie folk scene with a sound that blends traditional folk instrumentation with contemporary indie rock influences.

properties.cultural_impact: The Head and the Heart have contributed significantly to the resurgence of indie folk music in the 2010s, influencing a wave of similar artists and bringing folk-inspired sounds to mainstream audiences through their heartfelt and accessible music.
properties.performance_style: The Head and the Heart are known for their energetic and engaging live performances that balance intimate acoustic moments with dynamic full-band arrangements, creating a captivating experience for audiences.
